title: ApolloIQ - Search Relevance Engine Hosted API Demo
meeting_header: Date: 2026-10-21 · Start: 16:00 UTC · Duration: 48m · Attendees: Emma Cho, Daniel Park (Redwood) — Sara Malik, Tom Reyes, Priya Nair (ApolloIQ)
summary: Intro + hosted API demo focused on embeddings + reranker endpoints. Walked through Console, live API calls, and Redwood Optimize suggestions (batching, quantization). Discussed latency vs cost tradeoffs, VPC/private considerations, SOC2/KMS questions. Agreed next steps: send pricing/throughput sheet, security whitepaper, and kickoff POC planning once ApolloIQ provides sample dataset and QPS estimates.
action_items: Emma Cho: Share pricing and throughput comparison spreadsheet by 2026-10-23
Daniel Park: Provide simple cURL and SDK examples for reranker and embeddings within 48 hours
Tom Reyes: Share sample dataset (1000 docs) and expected QPS by 2026-10-25
next_steps: Send security & SOC2 whitepaper + KMS integration docs
Run quick hosted throughput test once sample data received
transcript:
[00:00] Emma: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Emma Cho from Redwood, AE on the account. With me is Daniel Park, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Sara: Good, thanks. Excited to see how this could slot into our search infra.
[00:10] Daniel: Awesome. Quick agenda: we'll do a 10-15 minute walkthrough of the hosted embeddings endpoint, then switch to the reranker demo — two-stage retrieval — and finish with the Console + Optimize tips and Q&A.
[00:23] Priya: Works for us. We really want to understand latency/cost tradeoffs and what a POC would look like.
[00:30] Emma: Perfect, that's what we'll focus on. Just to confirm, Tom you mentioned 10 qps steady, spikes up to ~200 qps during campaign windows?
[00:38] Tom: Yeah roughly, right now our in-house infra peaks at 150-200, but average is low. The main blocker is cost and complexity of maintaining the rerankers.
[00:47] Emma: Got it. Ok Daniel, demo time.
[00:50] Daniel: Cool. I'm sharing my screen — apologies if the screen share looks compressed — I'll start with the Console. So here's the model catalog, we preselect a curated embedding family for semantic search, you can choose between float16 and 8-bit quantized runtimes depending on cost/latency.
[01:06] Daniel: If we switch to the embeddings endpoint, you'll see the sample request. It's a simple POST: /v1/embeddings with a payload of text. Response returns a dense vector. I'm going to run an example against a small product dataset.
[01:22] [01:22] Sara: Quick question — do you recommend generating embeddings at ingest time or on read?
[01:26] Daniel: Good question. For ApolloIQ's pattern, if docs are mostly static, ingest-time embedding is cheaper overall. We also support on-the-fly caching (KV cache / prefix cache) so you can hybridize — generate on ingest and fallback to cached embeddings when reading.
[01:40] Tom: How's the storage for embeddings handled — is that part of Redwood or do we push to our vector DB?
[01:45] Daniel: You can do either. A lot of teams push to their vector DB (Pinecone, Milvus, or self-hosted) and call our embeddings API for generation. Redwood also offers an optional managed storage integration in Hosted mode that keeps vector metadata linked and simplifies reranker calls.
[01:58] Emma: For the two-stage flow, we recommend retrieve -> rerank. Daniel will demo the reranker endpoint now.
[02:05] Daniel: Switching context — reranker endpoint accepts a candidate list of doc ids with their context or embeddings plus the query, and returns a ranked list with scores and optional structured metadata. I'm going to call it with the top 10 retrieved candidates from the vector DB.
[02:22] [02:22] Daniel: Running the call... (typing) — ok response back in 120ms for this small test, reordering the list based on context relevance and model signals.
[02:30] Priya: 120ms — that's great. Is that end-to-end including the retrieval call?
[02:33] Daniel: This 120ms is pure reranker latency for the model variant we selected — low-latency optimized kernel on a GPU. Retrieval separately depends on your vector DB, but in our hosted flow you can co-locate retrieval which reduces total E2E.
[02:46] Sara: What about batching? If we have a burst of 200 qps, will reranker batch requests to be cheaper?
[02:53] Daniel: Yep, Redwood's serving runtime supports dynamic continuous batching that groups concurrent small rerank requests up to a latency SLO you define. You can set a max-latency-of-batch policy — e.g., 50ms extra — to trade cost for latency. Our Optimize module will also recommend batching and cache TTLs based on observed traffic.
[03:10] Tom: Does that mean in some cases tokens are delayed by batching and affect UX?
[03:14] Daniel: Right, that's the trade. The Console shows token-level latency and cost breakdown, so you can measure exactly how much batching saved you and what latency penalty it incurred.
[03:25] Emma: Another feature — automatic fallback models. If your chosen low-cost quantized variant falls below perf SLOs under load, traffic can be routed to a higher-capacity variant automatically.
[03:35] Sara: That fallback behavior — can we control routing by region? We need EU-only processing for some customers.
[03:41] Daniel: Absolutely. Smart routing policies allow you to prefer region, cost tier, or latency. For EU residency we recommend dedicated region pinning or Private (VPC) deployment.
[03:52] Priya: On Private deployments — what's the shortest lead time?
[03:55] Emma: Private deployments usually take more coordination — a few weeks for VPC set up and KMS integration; on-prem air-gapped is longer. For the POC we usually recommend Hosted with strict RBAC and VPC peering where possible.
[04:08] [04:08] Tom: Security — how does Redwood handle PII? We need SOC2 plus at-rest encryption with our KMS keys.
[04:14] Daniel: We support customer-managed KMS and envelope encryption for Private and Dedicated customers, and in Hosted mode we provide KMS integration partners and audit logs. We'll attach the SOC2 whitepaper after the call.
[04:25] Sara: Great. Back to the reranker — can it take structured tool outputs? For example, a price field and stock count?
[04:32] Daniel: Yes — the reranker accepts arbitrary structured context, we pass that into the model as context tokens or embeddings depending on configuration. You can also use function-calling style structured output if you want strict fielded results.
[04:45] Emma: I'm going to flip to the Console analytics — here you can see per-route token counts, median latency, and recent regressions flagged by our quality monitoring. Optimize suggests quantization levels and batching thresholds and shows estimated savings.
[04:59] Daniel: I'll run a quick 'simulate' in Console — this uses your sample traffic profile and recommends a quantization profile that trades 6-8% quality for ~30% cost savings for this workload. That suggestion includes which kernels to target and whether to enable KV prefix caching.
[05:15] Tom: How do you measure quality drop with quantization? We're worried about relevance regressions.
[05:20] Daniel: We run small eval suites on your prompt set as part of the POC — Redwood Optimize will score generation and reranker outputs against your labeled set and flag regressions. You can pin model versions and the Console supports canary rollouts to validate.
[05:32] [05:32] Priya: For the POC success metrics — what are typical thresholds?
[05:35] Emma: Commonly teams target parity within 1-2% of current relevance or a clear CTR improvement, and cost/latency improvements of 20-30% depending on starting point. We'll help you pick evaluation prompts.
[05:47] Sara: Ok good. Can you walk me through a sample API retry/fallback flow — say reranker times out?
[05:54] Daniel: Sure. The default is client retry with exponential backoff. On the server side you can configure fallback to a cheaper model variant or to a last-known-good cached ranking. We also emit traces to the Console so you can see where the latency happened.
[06:08] Tom: What's the typical SLA for hosted reranker latency?
[06:12] Emma: We publish model-level SLOs in the catalog; typical low-latency variants are 80-200ms per rerank for median depending on candidate count. We can commit SLA for Dedicated.
[06:25] [06:25] Daniel: I'm going to demo a quick end-to-end example: ingest text -> create embeddings -> store in vector DB -> retrieve top K -> call reranker with context. (types) Ok I'm running it against a 1k doc sandbox.
[06:40] Daniel: The embeddings call returned in 35ms, the vector DB lookup took 60ms (local), reranker 140ms — end-to-end ~235ms for a single query in this env.
[06:51] Sara: Nice. What about cost — do you charge per embedding vector generation and per rerank call?
[06:56] Emma: Hosted pricing is usage-based: embeddings per unit (per-embed) and reranker per-call or per-token depending on variant. We'll share a detailed cost sheet. For heavy throughput we recommend Dedicated capacity with reserved commitments to lower unit costs.
[07:09] Priya: If we do ingest-time embeddings and store them, does that reduce cost much?
[07:13] Daniel: Yes, upfront embed compute cost then cheaper per-query since you only run retrieval and sometimes rerank. But rerank still uses model compute; Optimize can recommend when to skip rerank via confidence thresholding to save cost.
[07:27] Tom: Can we run A/B tests for reranker variants?
[07:29] Emma: Yes — Console supports rollout policies and A/B experiments with traffic split and metrics collection. You can tie experiments to the quality monitoring alerting.
[07:39] [07:39] Priya: About integrations — we use SSO via Okta, and GitHub for infra.
[07:44] Daniel: SSO via SAML/Okta is supported; role-based access control maps to your groups. We can also integrate with GitHub for infra-as-code deployment configs for Dedicated.
[07:55] Sara: Any examples of customers in retail using this for product search?
[07:58] Emma: Yes, we've worked with several mid-market retailers — one saw a 22% CTR increase after moving to a two-stage pipeline with our reranker and Optimize-tuned quantization.
[08:09] Daniel: Back to the Console — I'm going to open the rollouts panel to show canary config and a simple policy: if ratio of warnings > 5% in canary, automatically revert.
[08:20] [08:20] Tom: Nice. For the POC scope — what do you need from us to start?
[08:24] Emma: Sample dataset (~1K - 10K docs), current reranker or baseline outputs if available, expected traffic profile (qps, peak), and the list of evaluation queries or critical flows. Tom said he'd share the sample by 10/25.
[08:36] Tom: Yep I can prepare that.
[08:38] Priya: Timeline for a small POC?
[08:40] Emma: Typical POC is 2-4 weeks — week 0 onboarding + ingestion, week 1 run baseline + initial optimize suggestions, week 2 tuning and canary, week 3 wrap-up. We'll adjust to your calendar.
[08:53] [08:53] Sara: Ok final set of questions — data residency and logs, do you redact PII automatically?
[08:59] Daniel: We provide configurable PII redaction rules in the ingestion layer; for Hosted we can enable automated redaction and only store hashes if required. Audit logs are available and can be forwarded to your SIEM.
[09:11] Emma: Great. Let's do a quick recap and assign action items.
[09:14] Emma: Next steps: we'll send pricing, SOC2/KMS docs, and a short POC plan. Tom will send dataset and traffic numbers. Daniel will share SDK examples and the reranker sample cURL.
[09:25] Sara: Sounds good. One more question, competitor angle: if we already use Pinecone for vector storage and OpenAI for embeddings, what's the migration story?
[09:33] Daniel: You can incrementally switch: keep vector storage and start hitting Redwood for embeddings, or use Redwood only for reranker while leaving your embeddings pipeline. We provide tooling to compare embeddings similarity matrices and a migration playbook.
[09:46] Priya: Thanks everyone.
[09:48] Emma: Thanks, we'll follow up with the docs and schedule the kickoff. Appreciate your time.
[09:53] Tom: Thanks.
[09:55] [END]
